title: New-Hire Onboarding
description: The most important things to know in your first week shipping Quiz Lab.

questions.prompt: Where do quiz pack JSON files live in the repo?
questions.explanation: Packs are single JSON files in app/src/lib/data/packs/, one file per pack; the packs index picks them up automatically (Pack Authoring Guide; Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: Where is the live Quiz Lab app hosted?
questions.explanation: The app is a static site served from GitHub Pages under the base path /product-demo. There is no Vercel deployment — that claim only appears in aspirational marketing copy (Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: What actually triggers a production deploy of Quiz Lab?
choices: Running a manual `npm run deploy` command
Merging a PR to `main`, which a GitHub Actions workflow builds and publishes
Clicking 'Promote to Production' in a hosting dashboard
questions.explanation: The entire pipeline is: merge to main → GitHub Actions builds the static site → it publishes to GitHub Pages. There is no separate deploy step or manual release (Engineering Handbook; Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: What database does Quiz Lab use to store packs and leaderboards?
choices: None — it is a fully prerendered static app with no backend
questions.explanation: Quiz Lab has no server runtime and no database; all content ships in the build as static files. Any mention of Postgres or a backend is outdated or marketing material (Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: Which framework and build setup does Quiz Lab use?
choices: Plain React with a custom Express server
questions.explanation: Quiz Lab is a SvelteKit app built with Vite and the static adapter; everything is prerendered at build time, so there is no server runtime (Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: How does new code reach the `main` branch?
choices: Through a reviewed pull request that is squash-merged
Pushed to a release branch and cherry-picked
Emailed to a maintainer who applies the patch
questions.explanation: The team practices trunk-based development: you never commit directly to main — all work lands through a reviewed, squash-merged pull request (Engineering Handbook).

questions.prompt: How many reviewer approvals does a PR need before it can merge?
questions.explanation: Every PR needs one reviewer approval before merge (Engineering Handbook, Review standards).

questions.prompt: What must pass in `app/` before a pack PR can merge, since a failure blocks the Pages deploy?
questions.explanation: `npm run build` (in app/) must succeed with the new pack registered; a broken build blocks the GitHub Pages deploy (Architecture Overview; Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: Which development model best describes how the team works?
choices: Gitflow with long-lived develop and release branches
questions.explanation: The team practices trunk-based development: main is always releasable and branches are short-lived, opened as small PRs and reviewed within a day (Engineering Handbook).

questions.prompt: How many choices must each quiz question have?
questions.explanation: The Pack Authoring Guide requires exactly 4 options in each question's `choices` array.

questions.prompt: How is the correct answer for a question stored in a pack?
choices: As a `correct` string holding the answer text
As a `correctIndex` integer from 0 to 3 indexing into `choices`
By marking the choice object with `isCorrect: true`
As the first item in the `answers` array
questions.explanation: Each question stores `correctIndex`, an integer 0–3 that indexes into the four `choices`. Storing the answer as a string is the deprecated v0 format and is no longer valid (Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: How many questions should a pack contain?
questions.explanation: The Pack Authoring Guide specifies 10–15 questions per pack, with mixed difficulty (1–3).

questions.prompt: Which sequence describes how work flows through Studio AI from start to ship?
choices: idea → tasks → pick up task → branch → PR → review → merge → done
questions.explanation: Work flows idea → tasks → pick up task → branch → PR → review → merge (ships) → task done. Merging auto-transitions the task to done and ships to GitHub Pages (Studio AI SDLC & MCP Workflow).

questions.prompt: What is the single highest-leverage thing you can do for a coding agent's output quality?
choices: Give it the largest possible context dump of every document
Curate a small neighborhood (~5 docs) of the most relevant context at task pickup
Let it search the whole knowledge base on its own each time
Run it with no context so it stays unbiased
questions.explanation: Giving an agent a small, curated neighborhood (~5 docs) of the most relevant context up front is the cheapest, highest-leverage lever on quality; agents left to search wander, burn tokens, and drift off scope (Engineering Handbook; Studio AI SDLC & MCP Workflow).
